evidence.says: Heading: Clancy, John J. (John Joseph), 1937-2019. Sources include The old dispensation (1999), The invisible powers (1989), and a Washington University obituary. Publisher information and the book data sheet support birth year 1937. External identifiers include VIAF 225300455, GND 170735273, ISNI 0000000109548257, and Wikidata Q138790029.

Q112375223 is John J. Clancy, described as a business executive and humanities lecturer (1937–2019). Its LC identifier is n88122905; VIAF, GND and ISNI match LC. It gives birth year 1937 and death year 2019. The response for Q138790029 resolves to Q112375223.
The page redirect is explicitly from Q138790029 to Q112375223. LC therefore links to a redirect to the item being checked, rather than to a different person.

Washington University identifies John J. “Jack” Clancy as a lecturer in its Interdisciplinary Project in the Humanities, reports his death in 2019 at age 82, and describes his teaching in political and economic thought.

The NORC General Social Survey bibliography lists John Joseph Clancy, The old dispensation: Loyalty in business (1996), as a PhD in History and Business at Washington University in St. Louis. Author, title, year and institution match the supplied AHA dissertation record and connect it to the work cited by LC.

notes: The lc_links_other_item flag is explained by Q138790029 redirecting to Q112375223. Retain Q112375223. LC and Wikidata agree on birth year 1937; no birth-year correction is needed. The dissertation match is supported by the NORC bibliography and LC’s citation of the later book with the same title.
